h1.tagline: Based on a real Amazon test (asked in Spring Boot): a movie search that must follow 5 rules, with the logic spread over 4 files.
lookFor: Write each rule as one line. Then find the ONE place in the code that handles it.
`indexOf` gives 0 for the first item (counts as false) and -1 for 'not found' (counts as true). Use `includes`.
Search patterns need the `i` flag to ignore capitals, and special characters like `(` must be escaped.
`a || b ? x : y` runs as `(a || b) ? x : y`. Add brackets.
'At least' means `$gte`. `Number('abc')` is NaN and slips past `< 0` and `> 10`.

hints: What does `['title','director','genre'].indexOf('director')` give? Does it count as true?
bugs.cause: `indexOf` gives 0 for 'title' (false, so allowed) but 1 for 'director' (true, so rejected).

hints: How is the search pattern built? Does it ignore capitals?
What happens with `new RegExp('(500')`?
bugs.cause: No `i` flag, so 'nolan' doesn't match 'Nolan'. Special characters like `(` also crash it.
bugs.fix: Escape the text and add `$options: 'i'`. See the reference fix.

hints: Rule 3 says trim first. Where does the code trim?
bugs.cause: `q` is never trimmed, so '   ' is searched as three spaces and finds nothing.

hints: Add brackets the way JavaScript reads the line.
bugs.cause: The line runs as `(rating diff || title compare) ? 1 : -1`, so it only ever returns 1 or -1.

hints: The rule says 'at least'. Which operator is used?
Does `NaN < 0 || NaN > 10` catch 'abc'?
bugs.cause: `$gt` leaves out the exact rating. 'abc' becomes NaN, which passes the range check.
bugs.fix: Use `$gte` in the repo, and add `Number.isNaN(minRating) ||` to the check.

h2.tagline: Overselling the last item, half-finished orders, rounding errors, and retries that charge twice.
lookFor: Read → check → save in separate steps can clash with other requests. Do it in ONE step (the repo has a helper).
If an order fails halfway, undo what was already changed. Better: check everything first.
Money: `Math.round(x * 100) / 100`. Watch the brackets.
Header names are lowercase in `req.headers`. Use `req.get()` everywhere.

hints: What is `total * 100 / 100`?
bugs.cause: `Math.round(total * 100 / 100)` is just `Math.round(total)`, which rounds to whole rupees.

hints: Order [Echo x1, Cable x5]: what happens to the Echo before the Cable fails?
bugs.cause: Stock is reduced inside the checking loop. When item 2 fails, item 1 is already reduced.
bugs.fix: Check all items first. Then reduce stock, and put it back if anything fails.

hints: Both requests read stock = 1 before either saves.
Look at `decrementIfAvailable` in productRepo.
bugs.cause: Two buyers both see 1 left, both pass the check, and both buy.
bugs.fix: Use `productRepo.decrementIfAvailable` (one step). If it returns null, the item is sold out.

hints: Log the key that's saved and the key that's looked up.
bugs.cause: It reads with `req.get()` but saves with `req.headers['Idempotency-Key']`, which is undefined.
bugs.fix: Use `const key = req.get('Idempotency-Key')` for both, and only when it exists.

h3.tagline: Scrolling shows duplicates, 'mark all read' half works, deleted items still count, and anyone can delete anything.
lookFor: The next page starts AFTER the last item: `$lt`, not `$lte`.
`forEach(async ...)` doesn't wait. Use `await Promise.all(list.map(...))`.
Hidden-but-not-deleted items must be filtered out EVERYWHERE, counts included.
Every `/:id` change must check the item belongs to the user.
When nothing is left, `nextCursor` must be null.

hints: Should page 2 include the last item of page 1?
bugs.cause: `$lte` includes the cursor item again, so it shows twice.

hints: Compare the filter in `list` with the one in `countUnread`.
bugs.cause: The count forgets `deletedAt: null`.

hints: Does `forEach` wait for async work?
bugs.cause: The reply goes out before the saves finish.

hints: How do you know there's another page?
bugs.cause: `nextCursor` is always set, even on the last page.
bugs.fix: Ask for one extra item. If you get it, there's more. See the reference fix.

hints: Is `userId` used in `remove` at all?
bugs.cause: Anyone can delete any notification.
bugs.fix: `if (!n || n.userId !== userId || n.deletedAt !== null) throw new NotFoundError(...)`

h4.tagline: A rate limiter that never limits, puts every client in one bucket, and says 'wait 40,000 seconds'.
lookFor: If the limiter 'does nothing', log the key and the list of times.
`req.headers` uses lowercase names. `req.headers['X-Api-Key']` is always undefined.
Keep times NEWER than `now - window`. Say the comparison out loud.
Retry-After is in SECONDS, rounded up.
Blocked requests should not count.

hints: Log `hits` after the filter. What's kept?
We want the last 60 seconds: t > now - window.
bugs.cause: It keeps the OLD times and throws away the new ones, so the count never grows.

hints: Log the key. Is it what you expect?
bugs.cause: `req.headers['X-Api-Key']` is undefined, so all clients share one bucket.

hints: What unit is the difference of two times? What unit does Retry-After use?
bugs.cause: It sends milliseconds, but the header is in seconds.

hints: Is the time saved before or after the limit check?
bugs.cause: Blocked requests are counted too, so a client that keeps trying stays blocked forever.
bugs.fix: Check the limit first. Only save the time for allowed requests.

h5.tagline: Two people get the same seat, failed holds keep seats locked, old holds never expire, and late confirms go through.
lookFor: Taking a seat must be ONE database step that says 'only if free'.
If seat 3 fails, give back seats 1 and 2.
A hold that has run out of time counts as free.
Check the hold is still valid when confirming.

hints: Both read 'free' before either saves. Is there a one-step update?
bugs.cause: Read, check, then save. Two people slip in between.
bugs.fix: Per seat: `seats.findOneAndUpdate({ _id, status: 'free' }, { $set: { status: 'held', ... } })`. null = taken.

hints: If A2 is taken, what happened to A1?
bugs.cause: Seats are taken one by one, and nothing gives them back on failure.
bugs.fix: Remember taken seats. On failure, set them back to `free`.

hints: When is a 'held' seat actually free?
bugs.cause: Only `free` counts. Expired holds block the seat forever.

hints: Does confirm look at `heldUntil`?
bugs.cause: An old hold can still be confirmed.
bugs.fix: If the hold has run out of time, return 410.

h6.tagline: Payments ADD to the balance, retries add money twice, refunds can be bigger than the payment, and you can spend money you don't have.
lookFor: Balance = money in − money out. Check the sign for each type.
Something created INSIDE a function starts fresh on every call.
All refunds together must not be more than the payment.
Don't let the balance go below 0.

hints: Does the sum in `balance()` look at `type`?
bugs.cause: Payments are added instead of taken away.

hints: Where is `seen` created? How long does it last?
bugs.cause: The `seen` map is created inside the function, so it's empty every time.
bugs.fix: Save the key on the ledger entry and look it up there.

hints: Does refund look at earlier refunds?
bugs.cause: Nothing compares refunds with the payment.
bugs.fix: Add up earlier refunds. If earlier + new > payment, return 400.

hints: Is the balance checked before paying?
bugs.cause: You can pay more than you have.
bugs.fix: `if ((await balance(walletId)) < amount) throw new HttpError(409, 'insufficient funds')`

h7.tagline: Two workers grab the same job, the newest job runs first, anyone can finish anyone's job, and crashed jobs never restart.
lookFor: Taking a job must be ONE step: 'queued' → 'running'.
Queues run oldest first.
Only the worker holding a job can finish it.
A running job whose time is up can be taken again. Check the comparison.

hints: Between `find` and `updateById`, can another worker get in?
bugs.cause: Two workers read the same queued job and both take it.

hints: Read the sort.
bugs.cause: It sorts newest first.
bugs.fix: Oldest first (the one-step claim already picks the oldest).

hints: Does `complete()` look at `worker`?
bugs.cause: Any worker can finish any job.

hints: When can a running job be taken again: before or after its time is up?
bugs.cause: It takes jobs that are still in use and never takes timed-out ones.

h8.tagline: The max price wipes out the min price, the total counts only one page, brand needs exact capitals, and page 0 shows the last page.
lookFor: Setting `filter.price = ...` twice replaces the first one. Combine them.
Count the total BEFORE cutting it into pages.
Exact match that ignores capitals: anchored pattern with the `i` flag.
`slice(-3)` counts from the END. Check page ≥ 1 first.

hints: Log the filter for `?minPrice=100&maxPrice=500`.
bugs.cause: The second line replaces the first, so the minimum is lost.
bugs.fix: Build both into one object: `{ $gte: min, $lte: max }`.

hints: Which list's length becomes total?
bugs.cause: It counts the page, not all matches.

hints: Saved as 'Apple'. Does 'apple' match?
bugs.cause: Plain equality cares about capitals.
bugs.fix: Use an anchored pattern with `$options: 'i'`. See the reference fix.

hints: skip = (0 − 1) × 3 = ? What does slice do with a negative start?
bugs.cause: A negative start counts from the end.

h9.tagline: The admin page is open to everyone, every token looks expired, any signature passes, and demoted admins keep their powers.
lookFor: Express runs things in order. A route written ABOVE `app.use(auth)` skips the login check.
Token `exp` is in SECONDS. `Date.now()` is in ms.
A signature check must COMPARE the two signatures, not just check one exists.
Read roles from the database, not from the token.

hints: Is the admin route above or below `app.use(auth)`?
bugs.cause: The route is set up before the login check, so it never gets checked.

hints: `exp` is in seconds. What is `clock.now()`?
bugs.cause: A ms number is always bigger than a seconds number, so every token looks expired.

hints: What is compared to what?
bugs.cause: It only checks both exist, so any signature passes.

hints: Where does `req.user.role` come from?
bugs.cause: The role comes from the token, which still says 'admin' after a demotion.
bugs.fix: Load the user by `payload.sub` and use the database role (401 if they're gone).

h10.tagline: Commas inside quotes break rows, error line numbers are wrong, '1,200' becomes 1, and duplicates get in.
lookFor: `split(',')` breaks text like "Shah, Ankit". Read the line character by character.
Line numbers should match the file: the header is line 1.
`parseInt('1,200')` is 1. Remove the commas, then use `Number()`.
Skip duplicate emails (ignore capitals) and empty lines.

hints: How does `parseLine` split fields?
bugs.cause: `split(',')` also splits on commas inside quotes.
bugs.fix: Go character by character and track whether you're inside quotes. See the reference fix.

hints: The header is line 1. What is the index of the first data row?
bugs.cause: It uses the list position (starting at 0, header not counted).

hints: What does `parseInt` do when it hits a comma?
bugs.cause: `parseInt('1,200')` stops at the comma and gives 1.
bugs.fix: `Number(raw.replace(/,/g, ''))`, then check it's a real number.

hints: Is there a list of emails already seen? What does a last empty line become?
bugs.cause: Repeat emails are saved again, and empty lines become errors.
bugs.fix: Skip empty lines. Keep a Set of lowercase emails and count repeats as skipped.

h11.tagline: Signups at the same time go past the reward limit, lowercase codes fail, failed signups still pay rewards, and a bad code blocks signup.
lookFor: Limits with many requests at once: use ONE step with `{ rewards: { $lt: 3 } }` + `$inc`.
Give rewards only AFTER the signup works.
Codes: trim and make uppercase.
An optional extra (a code) shouldn't block the main action (signup).

hints: The check and the increase are separate steps.
bugs.cause: Four signups all read 2 rewards, all pass, and all add one.

hints: Which comes first: the duplicate email check or the reward?
bugs.cause: The reward is paid before the signup is checked.
bugs.fix: Check and create the user first, then pay the reward.

hints: How are codes saved?
bugs.cause: Codes are saved in capitals, so 'ravi100' isn't found.

hints: The rule says an unknown code is ignored.
bugs.cause: A bad code stops the signup.
bugs.fix: Treat an unknown code as 'no code' and still create the user.

h12.tagline: Date keys sort wrong, empty days disappear, the last day is cut off, and the overall average is wrong.
lookFor: Dates must be 'YYYY-MM-DD' with leading zeros. `toISOString().slice(0, 10)` does this.
Charts need every day, even empty ones. Make the list of days first.
'From/to' dates usually include both ends.
Overall average = total time / total sessions, not the average of daily averages.

hints: How is `dayKey` built? Does 9 become 09?
bugs.cause: '2026-3-10' comes before '2026-3-9' as text, and it doesn't match the required format.

hints: Where do the days come from: the data or the date range?
bugs.cause: Only days with data are listed.
bugs.fix: Loop day by day from `from` to `to`, and use 0 for empty days.

hints: Are sessions on the `to` day included?
bugs.cause: `ts < Date.parse(to)` stops at the START of the last day.

hints: Day A: 1 session of 100s. Day B: 3 sessions of 10s. What's the real average?
bugs.cause: A day with 1 session counts as much as a day with 100.
